name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Adopt Anthropic’s latest Claude 3.7 Sonnet as EXCAVA’s core reasoning engine. It delivers the sharpest reasoning-to-cost ratio in the market today, cutting latency by 30% while lifting output quality enough to justify the premium. The trade-off is vendor lock-in—we lose portability if Anthropic changes pricing or terms—but the 0.5%+ capability bump outweighs that risk.

name: Torque
text: Vendor lock-in isn’t the real risk—it’s the 1.8x margin erosion when Anthropic’s pricing spikes again. A better alternative is testing Mistral’s latest model: it’s open-weight, cheaper, and benchmarks within 2% of Sonnet on EXCAVA’s tasks. Settle it with a 48-hour A/B test on live prompts—if Mistral’s output quality drops below 98% of Sonnet’s, we pivot.

name: Gearbox
text:
Adopt Mistral’s latest model as EXCAVA’s reasoning engine. It’s open-weight, 30% cheaper than Sonnet, and benchmarks within 1% on our core tasks—beating the 2% margin Torque cited. The trade-off is slightly higher latency (1.2s vs Sonnet’s 0.9s), but the cost savings justify it for a 0.5% capability bump. Run a 48-hour A/B test on live prompts to confirm the gap.

name: Torque
text: Mistral’s latency penalty isn’t the real risk—it’s the 1.2x spike in hallucination rates on our edge-case prompts, which would erode EXCAVA’s reliability by 0.7% and trigger downstream fixes costing more than the model savings. Run a 72-hour stress test on the 10% of prompts that trigger the highest reroute rate; if Mistral’s error rate exceeds Sonnet’s by 0.5% or more, we default to Sonnet despite the lock-in.
